answer: Behavioral reef clustering. Agents' transaction graphs are periodically embedded; identities whose interaction neighborhoods overlap beyond a learned threshold are flagged as one operator. A nebula score aggregates shared timing, counterparties, and value patterns into a per-cluster suspicion value, and flagged clusters face delayed settlement. To evade, an attacker must sustain genuinely disjoint activity across each identity, a garden of separate histories that costs real liquidity and attention per account.
